clue.text: Trim tree

definitions.meaning: trim as an adjective means neat and smart in appearance

explanation.surface: An instruction to a gardener to cut back a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trim' reads as a verb, but it is the adjective meaning neat.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are synonyms: smartly neat in dress, and a kind of conifer.

clue.text: So hedge built to keep in initially pugnacious farm animal

indicators.note: to keep in means to hold inside, so the rebuilt hedge letters hold the next letter
built means constructed, so the letters of So hedge are put together anew
initially picks the first letter of pugnacious

explanation.surface: A hedge has been built to stop an aggressive farm beast escaping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'built' rearranges SO HEDGE into SHEEDOG; 'to keep in' puts P inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: This working dog herds sheep on farms, so it is an example of a farm animal.

clue.text: Starts to rig up ropes at location in the countryside

indicators.note: starts to means the first letters of each following word, from rig to location

explanation.surface: Beginning to set up ropes at a site out in the country.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes things relating to or located away from towns, in farmland and villages.

clue.text: Female cutting inch of woven material

indicators.note: cutting means slicing into, so the female letter goes inside the woven letters
woven means interlaced, so the letters of inch of are worked together into a new order

explanation.surface: A woman trims an inch off some woven fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'woven' rearranges INCH OF into CHIFON; 'cutting' puts F inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a light, sheer silk or nylon fabric, so an example of material.

clue.text: Eavesdrop I wager, craftily

indicators.note: doing something craftily means doing it cunningly, so the letters of the words before it are cunningly rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone bets that a person is listening in secretly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'craftily' rearranges the letters of I WAGER.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb this word is a British informal synonym for secretly listening in on a conversation.

clue.text: Lab gear reassembled for school subject

indicators.note: reassembled means put together again in a new way, so the letters of Lab gear are rearranged

explanation.surface: Laboratory equipment is put back together for a lesson.
explanation.definitionFit: This branch of mathematics using symbols is taught as a subject in schools.

clue.text: Philanderer, better advised around sultanate

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the better advised word wraps the sultanate

parts.note: wiser means better advised or more prudent
Oman is a sultanate in Arabia

explanation.surface: A womaniser would do better steering clear of a Gulf state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sultanate' points to Oman, an Arabian state ruled by a sultan; 'around' signals the wrapping.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe a man who has casual affairs with many women, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Short maxim about part of sundial

indicators.note: short means cut short, so the maxim loses its final letter

parts.note: a gnome is a pithy saying or maxim
on means about, as in a talk on a subject

explanation.surface: A brief saying concerning a piece of a sundial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' removes the last letter of GNOME, leaving GNOM.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the upright pin or blade of a sundial whose shadow shows the time.

clue.text: Tight young lady narrowly avoided collision

parts.note: tight in the sense of stingy with money is near, an old British usage
a miss is a young unmarried woman

explanation.surface: A drunk young woman only just escaped a crash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tight' suggests drunk, but here it means mean with money, which is NEAR in British usage.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names an incident in which a crash or accident was only just escaped.

clue.text: Old English court in leading dictionary (abridged version)

parts.note: a star is a leading performer

indicators.note: abridged means shortened, so the dictionary's name loses its last letter

parts.note: Chambers is a well-known British dictionary, much used by crossword setters

explanation.surface: An old English court is listed in a top dictionary's shortened edition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abridged version' removes the last letter of CHAMBERS, leaving CHAMBER.
explanation.definitionFit: This was a notorious English court of Tudor and Stuart times, abolished in 1641.

clue.text: Cured ham, and tripe

definitions.meaning: meat from the hind leg of a pig, cured like bacon
tripe in the slang sense is nonsense or rubbish talk

explanation.surface: A menu offering cured ham alongside offal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tripe' looks like more meat, but it means nonsense, a British slang sense of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is cured pork from the leg; the other is old British slang for humbug and nonsense.

clue.text: Gem in ring presented to friend

parts.note: a ring is round, the shape of the letter O
a pal is a friend

explanation.surface: A jewelled ring is given as a gift to a friend.
explanation.definitionFit: This milky iridescent stone is a precious gemstone.

clue.text: Fight dishonest sailor in South American port

parts.note: a fray is a fight or brawl
bent is slang for crooked or dishonest
OS is the abbreviation for ordinary seaman

explanation.surface: A brawl with a crooked seaman in a harbour town in South America.
explanation.walkthrough: FRAY BENTOS is a port on the Uruguay River in Uruguay, also famous in Britain as a brand of tinned pies.
explanation.definitionFit: The town is a river port in western Uruguay, in South America.

clue.text: Section of society running study group

parts.note: a machine that is running is working
a class is a group of students studying together

explanation.surface: A part of the community runs a study circle.
explanation.definitionFit: This names the social stratum of manual and wage labourers, one layer of society.

clue.text: Follow part of castle path

parts.note: the keep is the strong central tower of a castle
a track is a rough path

explanation.surface: Tracing a route along a castle path.
explanation.definitionFit: To monitor something's progress closely is to follow it, an idiomatic synonym.

clue.text: Very strong, all the players with club

parts.note: the cast is all the actors in a play
an iron is a golf club

explanation.surface: A team of players armed with a club are mighty.
explanation.definitionFit: Used figuratively, the phrase means rigidly firm and unbreakable, as in an unshakeable alibi.

clue.text: Ventilation aid in vehicle kept by former supporter

indicators.note: kept by means held inside, so the vehicle sits within the other pieces

parts.note: ex is a prefix meaning former
a fan is a supporter
a tractor is a farm vehicle

explanation.surface: An old fan keeps an air-moving device in their car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'former supporter' reads as one ex-fan, but its two words give separate pieces that 'kept by' splits open.
explanation.definitionFit: This device draws stale air or fumes out of a kitchen or bathroom, so it aids ventilation.

clue.text: Another malt, partly responsible for getting you warm

indicators.note: partly responsible for says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Another whisky is partly what makes you feel warm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'partly responsible for' points back to ANOTHER MALT, which holds the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Thermal clothing keeps in body heat, so it is what gets a wearer warm.

clue.text: Message about welcoming uniform consistency

indicators.note: welcoming means taking in, so the message and about pieces hold the uniform letter

parts.note: a text is a message sent by phone
re means about or concerning
U is uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A note mentioning a uniform that is consistent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'welcoming' puts U inside TEXTRE.
explanation.definitionFit: The feel or structure of a substance, as in a smooth sauce, is its consistency.

clue.text: Excitement caused by the short stream

indicators.note: short means cut short, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: the definite article as written
a rill is a small stream

explanation.surface: Delight brought about by a little brook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' removes the last letter of THE, leaving TH.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden feeling of pleasure and excitement is a synonym.

clue.text: There's much talk from me about fight involving milliner

indicators.note: involving means taking in, so the milliner is placed inside the other pieces

parts.note: C is the abbreviation of circa, about
to box is to fight with the fists
a hatter makes hats, as a milliner does

explanation.surface: A talkative person speaks of a scrap involving a hat-maker.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition speaks as the answer itself: 'me' is the person who talks a lot. 'involving' signals the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer is an informal name for someone who talks incessantly, so from them comes much talk.

clue.text: Shrewd signal saving time

indicators.note: saving here means keeping safe inside, so the time letter is held within the signal

parts.note: a cue is a signal to act or speak

explanation.surface: A clever signal that saves time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'saving' puts T inside CUE.
explanation.definitionFit: In an older sense the word means clever or sharp-witted, as in a cute move.

clue.text: Trainee forced to spend minutes in court

indicators.note: in places the shortened forced word inside the court letters
to spend means to use up and so lose, so the minutes letter is taken away

parts.note: made means forced, as in made him do it

explanation.surface: A young recruit is obliged to pass a while in court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to spend' signals losing the minutes letter, and 'in' the insertion into the court abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a young person training for the armed forces or police, so a trainee.

clue.text: Leader of delegation is member to win over

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, here of delegation

parts.note: an arm is a limb, one of the body's members

explanation.surface: The head of a delegation is a member sent to persuade.
explanation.definitionFit: To charm away someone's hostility is to win them round, an idiomatic sense.

clue.text: Plumper son's game

parts.note: a plumper person is a rounder one

explanation.surface: A rather fat son's favourite pastime.
explanation.walkthrough: ROUNDERS is a British bat-and-ball children's game, similar to baseball.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a team bat-and-ball game played in British schools, so a game by example.

clue.text: Expected Dutch portrait painter to accommodate current king

indicators.note: to accommodate means to house within, so the painter's name holds the next pieces

parts.note: Sir Peter Lely was a Dutch-born portrait painter at the English court
I is the symbol for electric current
K is the abbreviation for king, as in chess

explanation.surface: A Dutch portraitist is supposed to put up the reigning monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to accommodate' puts IK inside LELY.
explanation.definitionFit: Something probable is what is anticipated, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Attacked outside by church worker

indicators.note: outside says the attacking phrase goes around the next piece

parts.note: set on means attacked
X is the multiplication sign, read as by, as in 3 by 4

explanation.surface: Someone assaulted out in the street by a church employee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' puts SET ON around X.
explanation.definitionFit: This parish officer looks after a church and churchyard, often digging graves.
